48: ### Primary Detection Signal
49: 
50: Detect the **pipeline phase** first. The three phases are sequential and each has a distinct surface: EXTRACT hits the live URL, WRITE produces the markdown, VALIDATE checks fidelity. A fourth path — REPORT — renders visual artifacts from an existing pair.
51: 
52: Route here when `DESIGN.md`, `tokens.json`, style reference, CSS capture, validation, report generation, or source-of-truth provenance are measured artifacts from a live site or an existing extraction pair.
53: **Route here too, even with no live URL present, when a request explicitly names the `DESIGN.md`/"style reference" artifact this mode owns** (e.g. "generate a DESIGN.md style reference for X from this brief"). Resolving elsewhere on a brief-only technicality would skip this mode's own authoring-boundary refusal (`references/authoring-boundary.md`), the exact check that request needs.

55: Do not produce new visual direction from an extracted reference here. This skill only captures and validates measured values.

61: echo "$REQUEST" | grep -qiE 'example|gold.*standard|stripe|vercel|linear|supabase|reference.*format' && PHASE="STUDY"
62: # default for extract/write/url/crawl:
63: : "${PHASE:=EXTRACT_WRITE}"
64: 
65: # Tool readiness check
66: [ -d "backend/node_modules" ] && TOOL_READY=true || TOOL_READY=false
67: ```

145: # always-loaded DEFAULT_RESOURCE); no orphans. The examples/ pairs are reachable
146: # only under STUDY intent — they are study artifacts the writer reads, never copied.
147: RESOURCE_MAP = {
148:     "EXTRACT_WRITE": ["references/design-md-format.md", "references/writing-style-guide.md",
149:                        "references/color-role-taxonomy.md", "references/component-taxonomy.md",

153:                        "assets/source-of-truth-router-card.md"],
154:     "VALIDATE":      ["references/quality-checklist.md", "references/anti-patterns.md",
155:                        "references/design-md-format.md", "assets/cardinal-rules-card.md"],
156:     "REPORT":        ["references/design-md-format.md"],
157:     "RUN_WRAPPER":   ["references/extraction-workflow.md", "references/troubleshooting.md", "references/guided-run.md", "assets/cardinal-rules-card.md"],
158:     "STUDY":         ["references/design-md-format.md", "references/writing-style-guide.md",
159:                         "references/examples/stripe/DESIGN.md", "references/examples/stripe/writing-notes.md",
160:                         "references/examples/vercel/DESIGN.md", "references/examples/vercel/writing-notes.md",
161:                         "references/examples/linear/DESIGN.md", "references/examples/linear/writing-notes.md",
162:                         "references/examples/supabase/DESIGN.md", "references/examples/supabase/writing-notes.md",
163:                         "references/examples/editorial-exemplar.md"],
164: }
165: 
166: UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST = [
167:     "Confirm the pipeline phase: full extraction (URL → DESIGN.md), validation-only, report generation, or example study",
168:     "For any extraction, confirm the target URL is live and renders JavaScript",
169:     "Confirm the output paths for tokens.json and DESIGN.md before writing",
170:     "Verify tool readiness: cd backend && npm install && npx playwright install chromium",
171: ]
172: 
173: AMBIGUITY_DELTA = 1
174: 
175: def _guard_in_skill(relative_path: str) -> str:
176:     resolved = (SKILL_ROOT / relative_path).resolve()
177:     resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT)
178:     if resolved.suffix.lower() != ".md":
179:         raise ValueError(f"Only markdown resources are routable: {relative_path}")
180:     return resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix()
181: 
182: def discover_markdown_resources() -> set[str]:
183:     docs = []
184:     for base in RESOURCE_BASES:
185:         if base.exists():
186:             docs.extend(p for p in base.rglob("*.md") if p.is_file())
187:     return {d.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix() for d in docs}
188: 
189: def classify_intents(request: str):
190:     text = (request or "").lower()
191:     scores = {i: 0 for i in INTENT_SIGNALS}
192:     for intent, cfg in INTENT_SIGNALS.items():
193:         for kw in cfg["keywords"]:
194:             if kw in text:
195:                 scores[intent] += cfg["weight"]
196:     ranked = sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1], reverse=True)
197:     primary, top = ranked[0]
198:     if top == 0:
199:         return ("EXTRACT_WRITE", None, scores)
200:     secondary, second = ranked[1]
201:     if second > 0 and (top - second) <= AMBIGUITY_DELTA:
202:         return (primary, secondary, scores)
203:     return (primary, None, scores)
204: 
205: def route_design_md_resources(request: str):
206:     inventory = discover_markdown_resources()
207:     primary, secondary, scores = classify_intents(request)
208:     intents = [primary] + ([secondary] if secondary else [])
209:     loaded, seen = [], set()
210: 
211:     def load_if_available(rel: str):
212:         guarded = _guard_in_skill(rel)
213:         if guarded in inventory and guarded not in seen:
214:             load(guarded); loaded.append(guarded); seen.add(guarded)
215:

217:     if max(scores.values() or [0]) < 1:
218:         return {"intents": intents, "needs_disambiguation": True,
219:                 "disambiguation_checklist": UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST, "resources": loaded}
220:     for intent in intents:
221:         for rel in RESOURCE_MAP.get(intent, []):
222:             load_if_available(rel)
223:     return {"intents": intents, "intent_scores": scores, "resources": loaded}
224: ```

30: ## 2. OVERVIEW
31: 
32: ### Why This Skill Exists
33: 
34: AI agents invent colors, guess font sizes, approximate shadows and round spacing to plausible values. When you tell an agent to build a page that looks like Stripe, it fills the gaps with values that do not match the real site. A `DESIGN.md` extracted from the live CSS removes that failure: every hex code, font weight, border radius, box shadow and spacing value is copied verbatim from the running page. The agent codes against measured ground truth instead of hallucinating.

36: ### What It Does

38: The skill ships an embedded Playwright crawler that runs a three-phase pipeline:
39: 
40: - **Extract.** Crawls the target URL across five responsive viewports, collects every computed CSS value, clusters them with OKLCH delta-E and classifies each token by temporal stability (L1 permanent through L4 content).
41: - **Write.** Produces a v3 **Style Reference** `DESIGN.md`. The value-bearing token sections (`Tokens - Colors`, `Tokens - Spacing & Shapes`, `Surfaces` and the Quick Start CSS + Tailwind) are pre-rendered deterministically by `backend/scripts/formatters-v3.ts` and assembled by `backend/scripts/build-write-prompt.ts`. The AI authors the prose sections (intro, `Tokens - Typography`, Components, Do's and Don'ts, Elevation, Imagery, Layout, Agent Prompt Guide, Similar Brands). Every value it writes comes from a pre-rendered section or the FACTS block of locked values, so it never invents or concretizes a number.
42: - **Validate.** Checks hex accuracy, the v3 section set and a Quick-Start fidelity check.
43: 
44: A fourth optional phase renders HTML previews and visual-diff reports.
45: 
46: ### The Cardinal Rule
47: 
48: Every value in `DESIGN.md` traces back to a token in `tokens.json`. No estimation, no rounding, no invention and no approximation. Because the formatter emits the value tables and the typography and component numbers come verbatim from the FACTS block, the old "100rem where tokens say 100%" fabrication cannot happen. The Style Reference is a named, confident, restrained design-system handoff rather than the old mechanical extraction report. The hard guard is unchanged: never assert a system the data contradicts (no gradient-as-depth, no "focus is consistent" when it is not).

Inferred claims carry an `[INFERRED]` marker and cite the measured token they rest on. Absent values are stamped or omitted rather than backfilled. 12: 
13: # sk-design-md-generator
14: 
15: > Point this mode at any live website and get a measured v3 Style Reference `DESIGN.md`, so agents build against ground truth instead of invented colors, fonts, spacing and shadows.
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## 1. AT A GLANCE
20: 
21: | Aspect | What you get |
22: |---|---|
23: | **Use it for** | Extracting verified design tokens from any live URL into a machine-readable `DESIGN.md` that replaces guesswork with ground truth |
24: | **Invoke with** | "extract design system", "generate DESIGN.md", "capture website css", "design tokens from url", "validate design.md" or auto-routing on extraction keywords |
25: | **Works on** | Any publicly accessible URL that renders JavaScript. Needs Node 20 or newer, Playwright and Chromium (~500 MB one-time install) |
26: | **Produces** | A `tokens.json` with every measured CSS value and a v3 **Style Reference** `DESIGN.md` (a named, role-driven design-system handoff with copy-paste CSS and Tailwind), plus optional HTML reports and fidelity proofs |
27: 
28: ---
29: 
30: ## 2. OVERVIEW
31: 
32: ### Why This Skill Exists
33: 
34: AI agents invent colors, guess font sizes, approximate shadows and round spacing to plausible values. When you tell an agent to build a page that looks like Stripe, it fills the gaps with values that do not match the real site. A `DESIGN.md` extracted from the live CSS removes that failure: every hex code, font weight, border radius, box shadow and spacing value is copied verbatim from the running page. The agent codes against measured ground truth instead of hallucinating.
35: 
36: ### What It Does
37: 
38: The skill ships an embedded Playwright crawler that runs a three-phase pipeline:
39: 
40: - **Extract.** Crawls the target URL across five responsive viewports, collects every computed CSS value, clusters them with OKLCH delta-E and classifies each token by temporal stability (L1 permanent through L4 content).
41: - **Write.** Produces a v3 **Style Reference** `DESIGN.md`. The value-bearing token sections (`Tokens - Colors`, `Tokens - Spacing & Shapes`, `Surfaces` and the Quick Start CSS + Tailwind) are pre-rendered deterministically by `backend/scripts/formatters-v3.ts` and assembled by `backend/scripts/build-write-prompt.ts`. The AI authors the prose sections (intro, `Tokens - Typography`, Components, Do's and Don'ts, Elevation, Imagery, Layout, Agent Prompt Guide, Similar Brands). Every value it writes comes from a pre-rendered section or the FACTS block of locked values, so it never invents or concretizes a number.
42: - **Validate.** Checks hex accuracy, the v3 section set and a Quick-Start fidelity check.
43: 
44: A fourth optional phase renders HTML previews and visual-diff reports.
45: 
46: ### The Cardinal Rule
47: 
48: Every value in `DESIGN.md` traces back to a token in `tokens.json`. No estimation, no rounding, no invention and no approximation. Because the formatter emits the value tables and the typography and component numbers come verbatim from the FACTS block, the old "100rem where tokens say 100%" fabrication cannot happen. The Style Reference is a named, confident, restrained design-system handoff rather than the old mechanical extraction report. The hard guard is unchanged: never assert a system the data contradicts (no gradient-as-depth, no "focus is consistent" when it is not).
49: 
50: ### The Design-System Knowledge Layer
51: 
52: | Capability | What the skill knows how to operate |
53: |---|---|
54: | **Token extraction** | crawl any public URL across five viewports and record every computed CSS value into `tokens.json` with an L1-L4 stability class |
55: | **Value-bearing sections** | pre-render `Tokens - Colors`, `Tokens - Spacing & Shapes`, `Surfaces` and the Quick Start CSS + Tailwind deterministically from `tokens.json` |
56: | **Prose authorship** | author intro, `Tokens - Typography`, Components, Do's and Don'ts, Elevation, Imagery, Layout, Agent Prompt Guide and Similar Brands strictly from pre-rendered sections or the FACTS block |
57: | **Fidelity validation** | verify every hex against `tokens.json`, the v3 section set and the Quick-Start fidelity check before any completion claim |
58: 
59: ### The Authoring Boundary
60: 
61: A value can have one of four origins: measured (read off the page and present in `tokens.json`), brief-provided (supplied by the user, not the page), inferred (a grounded characterization of a measured value) or absent (never captured). Only measured values enter the token tables. They enter unlabeled, so an unlabeled value is a promise it was measured. Brief-provided values stay in prose as a stated intent. Inferred claims carry an `[INFERRED]` marker and cite the measured token they rest on. Absent values are stamped or omitted rather than backfilled. [`references/authoring-boundary.md`](./references/authoring-boundary.md) draws this line in full. [`assets/source-of-truth-router-card.md`](./assets/source-of-truth-router-card.md) is the fill-in card that sorts each value before writing. Both are boundary documentation, not new capability. Authoring a design from a brief alone, with no live site to measure, is forward-authoring and it stays out of scope for this mode. This skill captures an existing surface. A brief-only request is a different contract routed to the sibling authoring skill `sk-design`, never satisfied by loosening fidelity here.
62: 
63: ---
64: 
65: ## 3. QUICK START
66: 
67: **Step 1: Install dependencies.** From the skill root, run:
68: 
69: ```bash
70: cd .skilled/skills/sk-design/sk-design-md-generator/backend
71: npm install
72: npx playwright install chromium   # ~500 MB, one-time
73: ```
74: 
75: `npm install` finishes and the Chromium binary download completes. Expect about 500 MB on the first run.
76: 
77: **Step 2: Extract tokens from a live site.** Run this from the repo root, not from `backend/`. `extract.ts` refuses any `--output` that resolves inside the skill, so a relative spec-folder path resolves correctly only from the repo root.
78: 
79: ```bash
80: npx ts-node .skilled/skills/sk-design/sk-design-md-generator/backend/scripts/extract.ts https://stripe.com --fast --output specs/<track>/<packet>/output
81: # --fast crawls 5 pages at 8 concurrency. tokens.json is written to <--output>/.
82: ```
83: 
84: Success means `tokens.json` exists under the output directory with the measured values.
85: 
86: **Step 3: Write the v3 Style Reference `DESIGN.md`.** Read `references/design-md-format.md` and `references/writing-style-guide.md`. The value-bearing token sections (Colors, Spacing & Shapes, Surfaces, Quick Start) are pre-rendered by `backend/scripts/build-write-prompt.ts` (which runs `formatters-v3.ts` first). You author the prose sections, including `Tokens - Typography`, taking every value from those pre-rendered sections or the FACTS block, never typing a number by hand. Every hex, pixel, font-weight, shadow and radius still traces to `tokens.json`.
87: 
88: **Step 4: Validate before claiming completion.** Run from the repo root with the full script path:
89: 
90: ```bash
91: npx ts-node .skilled/skills/sk-design/sk-design-md-generator/backend/scripts/validate.ts DESIGN.md specs/<track>/<packet>/output/tokens.json
92: ```
93: 
94: Expected: zero hex mismatches, all required v3 sections present and the Quick-Start fidelity check passing (every Quick Start hex traces to tokens, with `--page-max-width` matching tokens).
95: 
96: ---
97: 
98: ## 4. HOW IT WORKS
99: 
100: ### The Schema and Study Layer
101: 
102: The generator resolves section requiredness, capability groups, semantic roles, formatter emission, prompt instructions and validation from one versioned `V3_SCHEMA`. Corpus signals can inform advisory strata, but they cannot change locked target facts and cannot downgrade target, schema, provenance or output failures. The optional STUDY step queries bounded cards, hydrates one generation-bound bundle and transforms it into inert structural observations before WRITE. Instruction-like content and source-specific literals are removed. Exact-value and normalized-span leak checks run at the draft boundary. Any hit discards the draft before a production retry without STUDY. Authority remains user brief and owned system, selected-mode judgment, target evidence and deterministic checks, corpus reference evidence, then transport output.
103: 
104: ### The Three-Phase Pipeline
105: 
106: ```
107: EXTRACT (Phase 1)
108:   Playwright crawls the URL across 5 viewports (mobile through wide desktop).
109:   Collects computed CSS: colors, typography, shadows, radii, spacing, CSS variables.
110:   Detects dark-mode palette, framework markers, icon system, motion tokens, a11y data.
111:   Each token tagged with a 4-layer stability class (L1 permanent through L4 content).
112:   Output: tokens.json at <--output>/.
113: 
114: WRITE (Phase 2)
115:   build-write-prompt.ts runs formatters-v3.ts to PRE-RENDER the value-bearing
116:   token sections deterministically (a hue+lightness color-namer plus token emitters):
117:   Tokens - Colors / Spacing & Shapes / Surfaces and the Quick Start CSS + Tailwind.
118:   The AI authors the prose sections (intro, Tokens - Typography, Components,
119:   Do's/Don'ts, Elevation, Imagery, Layout, Agent Prompt Guide, Similar Brands),
120:   taking every value from a pre-rendered section or the FACTS block, never by hand.
121:   Result: a v3 Style Reference DESIGN.md.
122:   L1 and L2 tokens go in main sections. L3 tokens get a "Subject to change" note.
123:   L4 tokens excluded entirely.
124: 
125: VALIDATE (Phase 3)
126:   validate.ts (v3-schema-aware) checks every hex in DESIGN.md matches tokens.json.
127:   Confirms the required v3 sections are present and non-empty.
128:   Runs a Quick-Start fidelity check: every Quick Start hex traces to tokens,
129:   and --page-max-width matches tokens.
130:   Verifies L1/L2/L3/L4 classification rules were followed.
131:   Output: pass/fail with per-error line references.
132: ```
133: 
134: ### Token Stability Classes
135: 
136: Each extracted token gets a stability classification that governs its presence in `DESIGN.md`:
137: 
138: | Class | Name | Description | In DESIGN.md? |
139: |---|---|---|---|
140: | L1 | Permanent | Brand identity (logo colors, brand typeface, core radii) | Main sections |
141: | L2 | System | Design-system tokens (semantic colors, spacing scale) | Main sections |
142: | L3 | Campaign | Temporary (hero gradients, seasonal accents) | With "Subject to change" annotation |
143: | L4 | Content | Image-derived, one-off, article-specific | Excluded |
144: 
145: The classifier in `backend/scripts/cluster.ts` is deterministic. Boundary tokens get the higher (more restrictive) class.
146: 
147: ### The Private Procedure Card
148: 
149: The maintainer-facing card in [`procedures/design-system-extraction.md`](./procedures/design-system-extraction.md) supports extraction evidence after the public `md-generator` mode is chosen. It is not a user-selectable route.
150: 
151: ### Extract Flags
152: 
153: Run from the repo root with the full script path so a relative `--output` resolves outside the skill:
154: 
155: ```
156: npx ts-node .skilled/skills/sk-design/sk-design-md-generator/backend/scripts/extract.ts <url> [options] --output specs/<track>/<packet>/output
157: 
158:   --fast                 5 pages, 8 concurrency (still captures interaction, recommended)
159:   --max-pages <n>        Max pages to crawl (default: 8)
160:   --concurrency <n>      Playwright concurrency (default: 5)
161:   --with-interaction     Capture hover, focus and active states (this is the default)
162:   --no-interaction       Opt out of interaction capture
163:   --fast-no-interaction  Fast crawl and skip interaction (the old --fast behavior)
164:   --no-dark-mode         Skip dark mode detection
165:   --wait-for <strategy>  Wait strategy: networkidle | css | selector:<css>
166:   --extra-urls           Additional URLs to crawl
167:   --merge-with <path>    Merge into an existing tokens.json
168:   --output <dir>         Output directory (REQUIRED, must resolve to a spec folder outside the skill)
169:   --insecure             Ignore HTTPS certificate errors (self-signed or staging hosts)
170:   --verbose              Detailed logging
171: ```
172: 
173: ### Post-Extraction Scripts
174: 
175: Run these from the repo root as well (or pass absolute paths):
176: 
177: ```bash
178: npx ts-node .skilled/skills/sk-design/sk-design-md-generator/backend/scripts/validate.ts <DESIGN.md> <tokens.json>      # Phase 3: validate
179: npx ts-node .skilled/skills/sk-design/sk-design-md-generator/backend/scripts/proof.ts <url> <tokens.json>                # Fidelity proof
180: npx ts-node .skilled/skills/sk-design/sk-design-md-generator/backend/scripts/report-gen.ts <tokens.json> <dir> <DESIGN.md>  # HTML report
181: npx ts-node .skilled/skills/sk-design/sk-design-md-generator/backend/scripts/preview-gen.ts <tokens.json> <dir>          # Visual preview
182: ```
183: 
184: ---
185: 
186: ## 5. INTEGRATION & NAVIGATION
187: 
188: ### When To Use This Skill
189: 
190: Reach for this skill when you need to extract a live website's real CSS into a `DESIGN.md`. Use it for:
191: 
192: - Building a hallucination-proof design reference for AI agents.
193: - Re-extracting after a redesign.
194: - Validating an existing `DESIGN.md` against its source tokens.
195: 
196: Skip it in these situations:
197: 
198: - You are **inventing** a new design direction (palette, type scale, anti-default critique). That is `interface`. This skill captures what exists. That skill creates what does not.
199: - The source is a Figma file (`mcp-figma`).
200: - The need is a screenshot or a visual preview (`mcp-chrome-devtools`).
201: - The URL is not publicly accessible or cannot render JavaScript.
202: 
203: ### Related Skills
204: 
205: | Skill | Relationship |
206: |---|---|
207: | `interface` | The design-judgment sibling. It invents new direction. This skill provides the measured ground truth it consumes. |
208: | `sk-code` | Consumes `DESIGN.md` as the implementation contract. The hallucination-proof source of truth for colors, fonts, spacing, shadows and radii. |
209: | `mcp-figma` | Extracts from Figma Desktop, not live URLs. Use when the source is a Figma file. |
210: | `mcp-chrome-devtools` | Browser inspection and visual preview. Not a structured extraction tool. |
211: 
212: ---
213: 
214: ## 6. TROUBLESHOOTING
215: 
216: | What you see | Why | Fix |
217: |---|---|---|
218: | `chromium is not installed` or a Playwright error | Chromium binary not downloaded | Run `npx playwright install chromium` from `backend/` (~500 MB, one-time) |
219: | Extraction times out or returns empty tokens | Site blocks automated crawlers or requires authentication | Try `--wait-for networkidle` or `--wait-for css`. A site that requires login is out of scope |
220: | Dark-mode section is missing | The site has no `prefers-color-scheme` media query or dark-mode CSS variables | This is expected. Include a dark-mode section only when `tokens.json` contains a detected dark palette |
221: | Validation reports hex mismatches | `DESIGN.md` contains values not in `tokens.json` | Re-read `tokens.json` and fix the mismatched values. Every hex must match verbatim |
222: | `ts-node: command not found` | Dev dependencies not installed | Run `npm install` from `backend/` |
223: 
224: ---
225: 
226: ## 7. FAQ
227: 
228: **Q: How is this different from curated design-system template libraries?**
229: 
230: A: Curated libraries cover about 70 fixed brands. This mode works on any URL you point it at, including your own product. The values are pixel-verified against the live CSS, not hand-written approximations. Every token gets a stability classification, so you know which values are permanent and which are campaign-level.
231: 
232: **Q: Can I extract from a site that requires login?**
233: 
234: A: No. The crawler needs a publicly accessible URL that renders JavaScript. Authenticated pages are out of scope.
235: 
236: **Q: Do I need to write `DESIGN.md` by hand?**
237: 
238: A: You guide it, but you don't type the values. Phase 2 (write) is the AI agent's job, working from `tokens.json` and the v3 Style Reference specification in `references/design-md-format.md`. `build-write-prompt.ts` pre-renders the value-bearing token sections (Colors, Spacing & Shapes, Surfaces, Quick Start) via `formatters-v3.ts` and hands the agent a FACTS block of locked values (including the type scale). The agent writes the prose sections, including `Tokens - Typography`, but takes every number from a pre-rendered section or the FACTS block, so no value is ever hand-copied. The skill validates the result.
239: 
240: **Q: What if I only want to validate an existing `DESIGN.md`?**
241: 
242: A: Run `validate.ts` standalone. It checks hex accuracy against `tokens.json`, the v3 Style Reference section set and the Quick-Start fidelity check (every Quick Start hex traces to tokens, with `--page-max-width` matching tokens). No re-extraction needed.
243: 
244: **Q: How does this relate to `interface`?**
245: 
246: A: This skill captures what exists on a live site. `interface` invents new direction. When an extraction feeds into designing new UI, load `interface` for the judgment and this skill for the ground truth.
247: 
248: ---
249:

253: |---|---|
254: | Tool dependencies installed | `ls backend/node_modules/playwright` returns a directory |
255: | Chromium available | `npx playwright install --dry-run chromium` from `backend/` shows installed |

14: # SKILL.md File Templates - Creation Guide
15: 
16: Templates for creating SKILL.md files with proper structure, frontmatter, and required sections.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Purpose of SKILL.md Files
23: 
24: SKILL.md files define AI agent skills - reusable capabilities that extend an agent's functionality for specific domains or workflows. A well-crafted SKILL.md:
25: 
26: - **Triggers automatically** when relevant patterns are detected
27: - **Guides the agent** through specialized workflows
28: - **Maintains consistency** across conversations
29: - **Encodes expertise** in specific domains
30: 
31: ### Template Overview
32: 
33: This guide provides **one comprehensive SKILL template** (Section 3) that covers all skill types from simple single-purpose tools to complex multi-mode orchestrators.
34: 
35: **The template is flexible:**
36: - **Simple skills**: Use required core sections only (WHEN TO USE, SMART ROUTING, HOW IT WORKS, RULES, REFERENCES)
37: - **Skills with bundled resources**: Say in Section 2 what selects the skill and what it loads first, and put the router in the sibling `ROUTER.md`. Use `references/`, `assets/`, and `scripts/`
38: - **Multi-mode skills**: Expand WHEN TO USE and HOW IT WORKS sections by mode
39: - **All skills**: Section 2 (SMART ROUTING) is required: 8 to 12 non-blank lines of plain prose
40: 
41: **Target size**: 800-2000 lines for SKILL.md (<5k words total)
42: 
43: **Examples**:
44: - Simple: Unit test generator, documentation formatter (no bundled resources)
45: - Moderate: API client, specialized code reviewer (with references and assets)
46: - Complex: Workflow orchestrator, document quality pipeline (multi-mode with extensive resources)
47: 
48: ### Progressive Disclosure Principle
49: 
50: SKILL.md architecture follows progressive disclosure:
51: 
52: 1. **Metadata** (YAML frontmatter) - Always in context (~100 words)
53: 2. **SKILL.md body** - When skill activates (<5k words)
54: 3. **Bundled resources** - Loaded as needed (unlimited size)
55: 
56: **Critical**: Keep SKILL.md <5k words. Move detailed content to `references/`, `scripts/`, or `assets/`.
57: 
58: ### Document Type Requirements
59: 
60: **Enforcement Level**: STRICT (SKILL.md files require perfect structure)
61: 
62: **Required Elements**:
63: - ✅ YAML frontmatter with required fields
64: - ✅ H1 title with subtitle
65: - ✅ Numbered H2 sections (ALL CAPS, integers only, never a letter suffix such as `2b.`)
66: - ✅ Section separators (`---`)
67: - ✅ No table of contents (forbidden in SKILL.md)
68: 
69: **Quality Targets**:
70: - Structure: 100/100
71: - Content quality: High (AI-evaluated)
72: - Overall: High (human/AI judgment)
73: 
74: ---
75: 
76: ## 2. FRONTMATTER REQUIREMENTS
77: 
78: ### Required Fields
79: 
80: | Field | Required | Format | Example |
81: |-------|----------|--------|---------|
82: | `name` | ✅ | hyphen-case | `my-skill-name` |
83: | `description` | ✅ | Single line, **≤ 130 chars** for skills (≤ 110 for commands), 1,536-char hard cap | `"Handles X when Y occurs"` |
84: | `allowed-tools` | ✅ | Array: `[Tool1, Tool2]` | `[Read, Write, Edit, Bash]` |
85: | `version` | ✅ | 4-part X.Y.Z.W | `1.0.0.0` |
86: 
87: > **Hard rules**: not a frontmatter key. They live in `hard-rules.json` beside the skill's `SKILL.md`, a JSON array of `{id, check, message, severity}` objects that the dispatch preflight reads.
88: 
89: > **Description budget & trim style**: see [`frontmatter-templates.md` § Description Budget & Trim Style](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md).
90: > Keep total project descriptions under the ~6,400-character ceiling. This leaves headroom below the 8,000-character auto-discovery limit.
91: > Drop product and stack lists. Drop marketing prose. Keep the skill name, primary verb, domain noun and mode suffixes (`:auto` or `:confirm`).
92: 
93: ### Template
94: 
95: ```yaml
96: ---
97: name: sk-example
98: description: Example workflow skill demonstrating proper frontmatter format with specific capabilities, use cases, and key differentiators for AI agent discovery.
99: allowed-tools: [Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep]
100: version: 1.0.0.0
101: ---
102: ```
103: 
104: ### Key Rules
105: 
106: - **name**: Must match folder name exactly, hyphen-case only
107: - **description**: Third-person voice, single line, no `<>` brackets
108: - **allowed-tools**: Use brackets `[...]`, not comma-separated string
109: - **hard rules**: Not a frontmatter key. They live in `hard-rules.json` beside `SKILL.md`, a JSON array of `{id, check, message, severity}` objects the dispatch preflight reads.
110: 
111: > **Complete Reference**: For validation rules, edge cases, array formats, and all document type frontmatter, see [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md)
112: 
113: ---
114: 
115: ## 3. SKILL TEMPLATE (WITH BUNDLED RESOURCES)
116: 
117: **Use for**: Skills with bundled resources (references, scripts, or assets)
118: 
119: **Target**: 800-2000 lines (SKILL.md <1000 lines, rest in resources)
120: 
121: **Size Constraints** (package_skill.py validation):
122: - Max 5000 words (3000 recommended)
123: - Max 3000 lines
124: 
125: **Required Sections**: WHEN TO USE, SMART ROUTING, HOW IT WORKS, RULES (with ✅ ALWAYS, ❌ NEVER, ⚠️ ESCALATE IF), REFERENCES (or combined `SMART ROUTING & REFERENCES`)
126: 
127: Packaging enforcement note:
128: - `package_skill.py` fails if `REFERENCES` is missing and no approved combined `SMART ROUTING & REFERENCES` structure exists.
129:

136: name: example-skill
137: description: Example skill demonstrating proper template structure with specific capabilities for semantic code search and context preservation workflows.

504: ### Section 2: SMART ROUTING (Required for All Skills)
505: 
506: **Purpose**: Use this section to explain how you route a request to this skill's resources.
507: 
508: **Three skill kinds, one shape**:
509: 
510: | Kind | How to tell | What Section 2 says |
511: |------|-------------|---------------------|
512: | Hub | the folder holds `mode-registry.json` and `hub-router.json` | how a prompt reaches a mode, and where the root `ROUTER.md` is |
513: | Mode packet | a packet folder inside a hub | what selects this packet, what it loads first, and where its own `ROUTER.md` is |
514: | Standalone | neither hub file | the same as a mode packet, with the router in its own `ROUTER.md` |
515: 
516: **The limit**: 12 non-blank lines and 180 words are the hard ceilings the check enforces. Aim for 8 to 12 lines. A packet or standalone skill says three things: what selects it, what it loads first, and where the machine router is.
517: 
518: **The sibling router**: the machine router lives in `ROUTER.md` beside `SKILL.md`, under a final `## MACHINE ROUTER` heading.
519: That heading is the one every reader parses. Its section number is optional, so `## MACHINE ROUTER` and `## 9. MACHINE ROUTER` both count, and the check ignores the number.
520: Keep pseudocode out of SMART ROUTING and put it in that section.
521: `SKILL.md` carries no `## MACHINE ROUTER` section of its own: two homes for one router is the dual declaration the check reports.
522: 
523: **The link line**: Section 2 names the router file with a relative markdown link, [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md), and its target resolves on disk. A sentence that mentions the name without a link fails, because a reader cannot follow it to a file that is not there.
524: 
525: **One router per folder**: every skill and every mode packet owns `ROUTER.md` inside its own folder, linked from its own `SKILL.md`. A router file whose real path leaves the folder is not that skill's router.
526: 
527: **The no-match outcome** is named `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK` everywhere. Low confidence returns a disambiguation checklist, never an empty result and never a guess.
528: 
529: **Validation**: `package_skill.py --strict` reports the routing shape with five codes:
530: 
531: | Code | Finding |
532: |------|---------|
533: | `RS-001` | SMART ROUTING is longer than the limit (12 lines or 180 words by default) |
534: | `RS-002` | `SKILL.md` carries a `## MACHINE ROUTER` section, with or without a code block |
535: | `RS-003` | A `## MACHINE ROUTER` section is not the last H2 of the document that holds it |
536: | `RS-004` | the skill has no sibling `ROUTER.md`, or its real path leaves the skill folder |
537: | `RS-005` | `SKILL.md` has no relative markdown link to `./ROUTER.md` that resolves |
538: 
539: The machine block itself is a fenced block or an unfenced run of indented lines.
540: It declares the router with one of these markers: `INTENT_SIGNALS =`, `RESOURCE_MAP =`, `DEFAULT_RESOURCE =`, `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST =`, `def discover_markdown_resources` or `def _guard_in_skill`.
541: A fence closes only on a run of the same character that is at least as long as its opening run.
542: 
543: **Known debt** is listed in `sk-create-skill/scripts/routing-shape-known-debt.json`.
544: Entries use skill paths relative to `.skilled/skills`, such as `sk-code/sk-code-review`.
545: A folder outside that root is never debt.
546: Each entry records `{"lines", "words", "machineBlocks", "codes"}`.
547: A listed skill fails if its line count, word count or machine blocks left in `SKILL.md` exceed the record, or if it adds an unrecorded code.
548: The checker ignores entries in any other form.
549: Remove an entry when the skill follows the canon.
550: 
551: **Placement**: the SMART ROUTING section sits after Section 1 (WHEN TO USE) and before HOW IT WORKS, and `ROUTER.md` sits beside `SKILL.md` at the skill root.
552: 
553: **Worked example** (a canon Section 2 and its sibling router, nothing else):
554: 
555: \## 2. SMART ROUTING
556: 
557: Use this skill for [domain] work: [trigger 1], [trigger 2], or [trigger 3].
558: The first signal is [project/stack/mode detection], because it picks the knowledge folder before any intent scoring.
559: Load `references/[default].md` first on every run. The other files assume it.
560: Then load what the matched intent maps to: [intent A] reads `references/[domain]/[a].md`, and [intent B] reads `assets/[domain]/[b].md`.
561: Keep every path inside this skill folder and load a file only when it exists.
562: When two intents score close together, follow both in rank order.
563: When nothing matches, report `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK` with the checklist from the machine router instead of guessing.
564: The machine router lives in [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md); read it before selecting a resource.
565: 
566: ---
567: 
568: The link resolves to the sibling file, whose one heading the readers parse is:
569: 
570: \## MACHINE ROUTER
571: 
572: ```python
573: DEFAULT_RESOURCE = "references/[default].md"
574: INTENT_SIGNALS = {"PRIMARY": {"weight": 4, "keywords": [("[keyword]", 4), ("[phrase]", 3)]}}
575: RESOURCE_MAP = {"PRIMARY": ["references/[domain]/[primary].md"]}
576: UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST = ["Confirm the routing key", "Confirm the intent", "Provide one concrete input"]
577: 
578: def route_[skill_name]_resources(user_request, task=None):
579:     inventory = discover_markdown_resources()
580:     primary, secondary, scores = classify_intents(user_request, task)
581:     if max(scores.values() or [0]) < 0.5:
582:         return {"load_level": "UNKNOWN_FALLBACK", "checklist": UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST}
583:     return {"routing_key": get_routing_key(task, [primary]), "resources": inventory}
584: ```
585: 
586: The full resilience pattern (guarded paths, recursive discovery, routing keys) is in [skill-smart-router.md](./skill-smart-router.md).
587: 
588: **Writing Tips**:
589: - Open Section 2 with the signal that actually picks this skill's files.
590: - Name the first file to load, so a reader knows where to start.
591: - Name the router file with a markdown link, so a reader can open it.
592: - Keep `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK` as the named no-match outcome.
593: - Edit `INTENT_SIGNALS` and `RESOURCE_MAP` in `ROUTER.md` when the skill gains a domain.
594: - Avoid duplicate lookup tables, static file inventories, and unguarded `load()` calls.
595: 
596: **Word Budget**: 8-12 non-blank lines of prose

14: # SKILL.md File Templates - Creation Guide
15: 
16: Templates for creating SKILL.md files with proper structure, frontmatter, and required sections.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Purpose of SKILL.md Files
23: 
24: SKILL.md files define AI agent skills - reusable capabilities that extend an agent's functionality for specific domains or workflows. A well-crafted SKILL.md:
25: 
26: - **Triggers automatically** when relevant patterns are detected
27: - **Guides the agent** through specialized workflows
28: - **Maintains consistency** across conversations
29: - **Encodes expertise** in specific domains
30: 
31: ### Template Overview
32: 
33: This guide provides **one comprehensive SKILL template** (Section 3) that covers all skill types from simple single-purpose tools to complex multi-mode orchestrators.
34: 
35: **The template is flexible:**
36: - **Simple skills**: Use required core sections only (WHEN TO USE, SMART ROUTING, HOW IT WORKS, RULES, REFERENCES)
37: - **Skills with bundled resources**: Say in Section 2 what selects the skill and what it loads first, and put the router in the sibling `ROUTER.md`. Use `references/`, `assets/`, and `scripts/`
38: - **Multi-mode skills**: Expand WHEN TO USE and HOW IT WORKS sections by mode
39: - **All skills**: Section 2 (SMART ROUTING) is required: 8 to 12 non-blank lines of plain prose
40: 
41: **Target size**: 800-2000 lines for SKILL.md (<5k words total)
42: 
43: **Examples**:
44: - Simple: Unit test generator, documentation formatter (no bundled resources)
45: - Moderate: API client, specialized code reviewer (with references and assets)
46: - Complex: Workflow orchestrator, document quality pipeline (multi-mode with extensive resources)
47: 
48: ### Progressive Disclosure Principle
49: 
50: SKILL.md architecture follows progressive disclosure:
51: 
52: 1. **Metadata** (YAML frontmatter) - Always in context (~100 words)
53: 2. **SKILL.md body** - When skill activates (<5k words)
54: 3. **Bundled resources** - Loaded as needed (unlimited size)
55: 
56: **Critical**: Keep SKILL.md <5k words. Move detailed content to `references/`, `scripts/`, or `assets/`.
57: 
58: ### Document Type Requirements
59: 
60: **Enforcement Level**: STRICT (SKILL.md files require perfect structure)
61: 
62: **Required Elements**:
63: - ✅ YAML frontmatter with required fields
64: - ✅ H1 title with subtitle
65: - ✅ Numbered H2 sections (ALL CAPS, integers only, never a letter suffix such as `2b.`)
66: - ✅ Section separators (`---`)
67: - ✅ No table of contents (forbidden in SKILL.md)
68: 
69: **Quality Targets**:
70: - Structure: 100/100
71: - Content quality: High (AI-evaluated)
72: - Overall: High (human/AI judgment)
73: 
74: ---
75: 
76: ## 2. FRONTMATTER REQUIREMENTS
77: 
78: ### Required Fields
79: 
80: | Field | Required | Format | Example |
81: |-------|----------|--------|---------|
82: | `name` | ✅ | hyphen-case | `my-skill-name` |
83: | `description` | ✅ | Single line, **≤ 130 chars** for skills (≤ 110 for commands), 1,536-char hard cap | `"Handles X when Y occurs"` |
84: | `allowed-tools` | ✅ | Array: `[Tool1, Tool2]` | `[Read, Write, Edit, Bash]` |
85: | `version` | ✅ | 4-part X.Y.Z.W | `1.0.0.0` |
86: 
87: > **Hard rules**: not a frontmatter key. They live in `hard-rules.json` beside the skill's `SKILL.md`, a JSON array of `{id, check, message, severity}` objects that the dispatch preflight reads.
88: 
89: > **Description budget & trim style**: see [`frontmatter-templates.md` § Description Budget & Trim Style](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md).
90: > Keep total project descriptions under the ~6,400-character ceiling. This leaves headroom below the 8,000-character auto-discovery limit.
91: > Drop product and stack lists. Drop marketing prose. Keep the skill name, primary verb, domain noun and mode suffixes (`:auto` or `:confirm`).
92: 
93: ### Template
94: 
95: ```yaml
96: ---
97: name: sk-example
98: description: Example workflow skill demonstrating proper frontmatter format with specific capabilities, use cases, and key differentiators for AI agent discovery.
99: allowed-tools: [Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep]
100: version: 1.0.0.0
101: ---
102: ```
103: 
104: ### Key Rules
105: 
106: - **name**: Must match folder name exactly, hyphen-case only
107: - **description**: Third-person voice, single line, no `<>` brackets
108: - **allowed-tools**: Use brackets `[...]`, not comma-separated string
109: - **hard rules**: Not a frontmatter key. They live in `hard-rules.json` beside `SKILL.md`, a JSON array of `{id, check, message, severity}` objects the dispatch preflight reads.
110: 
111: > **Complete Reference**: For validation rules, edge cases, array formats, and all document type frontmatter, see [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md)
112: 
113: ---
114: 
115: ## 3. SKILL TEMPLATE (WITH BUNDLED RESOURCES)
116: 
117: **Use for**: Skills with bundled resources (references, scripts, or assets)
118: 
119: **Target**: 800-2000 lines (SKILL.md <1000 lines, rest in resources)

122: - Max 5000 words (3000 recommended)

126: 
127: Packaging enforcement note:
128: - `package_skill.py` fails if `REFERENCES` is missing and no approved combined `SMART ROUTING & REFERENCES` structure exists.

138: allowed-tools: [Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep]

402: The router in `ROUTER.md` discovers reference, asset, and script docs dynamically. Start with `references/[primary].md`, `assets/[template].md`, and any skill-specific automation under `scripts/`, then load task-specific resources according to Section 2.
403: 
404: Scripts: `scripts/[primary-helper]` when the skill ships automation. Omit this line when no scripts exist.
405: 
406: Related skills: `[related-skill]` for [relationship], `[other-skill]` for [relationship], and `system-spec-kit` when packet documentation or memory continuity applies.
407: 
408: Install guide: [INSTALL-GUIDE.md](INSTALL-GUIDE.md) when the skill has installation or configuration steps.
409: 
410: ---
411: 
412: **Word Count Targets**:
413: - Section 1 (WHEN TO USE): 150-200 lines
414: - Section 2 (SMART ROUTING): 8-12 non-blank lines of plain prose (the router block lives in the sibling `ROUTER.md`)
415: - Section 3 (HOW IT WORKS): 200-300 lines
416: - Section 4 (RULES): 150-200 lines
417: - Section 5 (REFERENCES): 40-120 lines
418: - Section 6 (SUCCESS CRITERIA): 80-120 lines
419: - Section 7 (INTEGRATION POINTS): 100-150 lines
420: - Section 8 (REFERENCES AND RELATED RESOURCES): 20-60 lines
421: 
422: **Bundled Resources Structure (Monolithic)**:
423: ```
424: .skilled/skills/skill-name/       # Note: .skilled/skills/ (singular, NOT skills)
425: ├── SKILL.md (800-1000 lines)
426: └── Bundled Resources
427:     ├── scripts/          - Executable automation
428:     ├── references/       - Detailed documentation (flat or domain subfolders)
429:     └── assets/           - Templates and examples (subfolders OK)
430:         ├── opencode/     - OpenCode component templates (skills, agents, commands)
431:         └── readme/        - README-shaped scaffolds (README, install guide)
432: ```
433: 
434: **Folder Organization Principle**:
435: - **references/** = flat for small skills, domain subfolders for medium/complex skills
436:   - Flat example: `references/core-standards.md`, `references/validation.md`
437:   - Domain example: `references/backend/go/`, `references/frontend/react/`
438: - **assets/** = Subfolders ALLOWED when organizing many files by category
439:   - Group related templates together
440:   - Example: `assets/skill/`, `assets/readme/`, `assets/flowcharts/`
441: - **scripts/** = Typically flat, but subfolders OK for large script collections
442: 
443: **Native Discovery**:
444: - Skills auto-discovered from `.skilled/skills/*/SKILL.md` frontmatter
445: - Skill name in frontmatter MUST match folder name
446: - Skills appear as `skills_<name>` functions in OpenCode (hyphens → underscores)
447: - Invoke via `Read(".skilled/skills/<name>/SKILL.md")`

503: 
504: ### Section 2: SMART ROUTING (Required for All Skills)
505: 
506: **Purpose**: Use this section to explain how you route a request to this skill's resources.
507: 
508: **Three skill kinds, one shape**:
509: 
510: | Kind | How to tell | What Section 2 says |
511: |------|-------------|---------------------|
512: | Hub | the folder holds `mode-registry.json` and `hub-router.json` | how a prompt reaches a mode, and where the root `ROUTER.md` is |
513: | Mode packet | a packet folder inside a hub | what selects this packet, what it loads first, and where its own `ROUTER.md` is |
514: | Standalone | neither hub file | the same as a mode packet, with the router in its own `ROUTER.md` |
515: 
516: **The limit**: 12 non-blank lines and 180 words are the hard ceilings the check enforces. Aim for 8 to 12 lines. A packet or standalone skill says three things: what selects it, what it loads first, and where the machine router is.
517: 
518: **The sibling router**: the machine router lives in `ROUTER.md` beside `SKILL.md`, under a final `## MACHINE ROUTER` heading.
519: That heading is the one every reader parses. Its section number is optional, so `## MACHINE ROUTER` and `## 9. MACHINE ROUTER` both count, and the check ignores the number.
520: Keep pseudocode out of SMART ROUTING and put it in that section.
521: `SKILL.md` carries no `## MACHINE ROUTER` section of its own: two homes for one router is the dual declaration the check reports.
522: 
523: **The link line**: Section 2 names the router file with a relative markdown link, [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md), and its target resolves on disk. A sentence that mentions the name without a link fails, because a reader cannot follow it to a file that is not there.
524: 
525: **One router per folder**: every skill and every mode packet owns `ROUTER.md` inside its own folder, linked from its own `SKILL.md`. A router file whose real path leaves the folder is not that skill's router.
526: 
527: **The no-match outcome** is named `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK` everywhere. Low confidence returns a disambiguation checklist, never an empty result and never a guess.
528: 
529: **Validation**: `package_skill.py --strict` reports the routing shape with five codes:
530: 
531: | Code | Finding |
532: |------|---------|
533: | `RS-001` | SMART ROUTING is longer than the limit (12 lines or 180 words by default) |
534: | `RS-002` | `SKILL.md` carries a `## MACHINE ROUTER` section, with or without a code block |
535: | `RS-003` | A `## MACHINE ROUTER` section is not the last H2 of the document that holds it |
536: | `RS-004` | the skill has no sibling `ROUTER.md`, or its real path leaves the skill folder |
537: | `RS-005` | `SKILL.md` has no relative markdown link to `./ROUTER.md` that resolves |
538: 
539: The machine block itself is a fenced block or an unfenced run of indented lines.
540: It declares the router with one of these markers: `INTENT_SIGNALS =`, `RESOURCE_MAP =`, `DEFAULT_RESOURCE =`, `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST =`, `def discover_markdown_resources` or `def _guard_in_skill`.
541: A fence closes only on a run of the same character that is at least as long as its opening run.
542: 
543: **Known debt** is listed in `sk-create-skill/scripts/routing-shape-known-debt.json`.
544: Entries use skill paths relative to `.skilled/skills`, such as `sk-code/sk-code-review`.
545: A folder outside that root is never debt.
546: Each entry records `{"lines", "words", "machineBlocks", "codes"}`.
547: A listed skill fails if its line count, word count or machine blocks left in `SKILL.md` exceed the record, or if it adds an unrecorded code.
548: The checker ignores entries in any other form.
549: Remove an entry when the skill follows the canon.
550: 
551: **Placement**: the SMART ROUTING section sits after Section 1 (WHEN TO USE) and before HOW IT WORKS, and `ROUTER.md` sits beside `SKILL.md` at the skill root.
552: 
553: **Worked example** (a canon Section 2 and its sibling router, nothing else):
554: 
555: \## 2. SMART ROUTING
556: 
557: Use this skill for [domain] work: [trigger 1], [trigger 2], or [trigger 3].
558: The first signal is [project/stack/mode detection], because it picks the knowledge folder before any intent scoring.
559: Load `references/[default].md` first on every run. The other files assume it.
560: Then load what the matched intent maps to: [intent A] reads `references/[domain]/[a].md`, and [intent B] reads `assets/[domain]/[b].md`.
561: Keep every path inside this skill folder and load a file only when it exists.
562: When two intents score close together, follow both in rank order.
563: When nothing matches, report `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK` with the checklist from the machine router instead of guessing.
564: The machine router lives in [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md); read it before selecting a resource.
565: 
566: ---
567: 
568: The link resolves to the sibling file, whose one heading the readers parse is:
569: 
570: \## MACHINE ROUTER
571: 
572: ```python
573: DEFAULT_RESOURCE = "references/[default].md"
574: INTENT_SIGNALS = {"PRIMARY": {"weight": 4, "keywords": [("[keyword]", 4), ("[phrase]", 3)]}}
575: RESOURCE_MAP = {"PRIMARY": ["references/[domain]/[primary].md"]}
576: UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST = ["Confirm the routing key", "Confirm the intent", "Provide one concrete input"]
577: 
578: def route_[skill_name]_resources(user_request, task=None):
579:     inventory = discover_markdown_resources()
580:     primary, secondary, scores = classify_intents(user_request, task)
581:     if max(scores.values() or [0]) < 0.5:
582:         return {"load_level": "UNKNOWN_FALLBACK", "checklist": UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST}
583:     return {"routing_key": get_routing_key(task, [primary]), "resources": inventory}
584: ```
585: 
586: The full resilience pattern (guarded paths, recursive discovery, routing keys) is in [skill-smart-router.md](./skill-smart-router.md).
587: 
588: **Writing Tips**:
589: - Open Section 2 with the signal that actually picks this skill's files.
590: - Name the first file to load, so a reader knows where to start.
591: - Name the router file with a markdown link, so a reader can open it.
592: - Keep `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK` as the named no-match outcome.
593: - Edit `INTENT_SIGNALS` and `RESOURCE_MAP` in `ROUTER.md` when the skill gains a domain.
594: - Avoid duplicate lookup tables, static file inventories, and unguarded `load()` calls.
595: 
596: **Word Budget**: 8-12 non-blank lines of prose
597:

643: **Purpose**: Add visual clarity to complex Python/YAML logic blocks without removing structured code

667: [Check Condition A]
668:   ↓
669: A True? ─── NO ──→ [Path B]
670:   │                    ↓
671:   │              [Process B]
672:   │                    ↓
673:   YES              [Continue]
674:   ↓
675: [Process A]
676:   ↓
677: RESULT
678: \`\`\`

680: **Implementation**:
681: \`\`\`python

683:     """Original Python logic preserved"""
684:     if condition_a:

686:     else:
687:         return process_b(input)
688: \`\`\`

697:   defaults:

699:     depth: 10

702: **Writing Tips**:
703: - **Keep code**: Don't remove Python/YAML - it's precise and complete
704: - **Add diagrams**: Flowcharts provide at-a-glance understanding
705: - **Placement**:
706:   - Flowchart FIRST if it aids comprehension before reading code
707:   - Flowchart AFTER if it summarizes complex code
708:   - Both before AND after for very complex logic
709: - **Consistency**: Use the same ASCII flowchart style as the other diagrams in the file
710: - **When to skip**: Simple 2-3 line logic doesn't need flowcharts

712: **Example Use Cases**:
713: - Mode detection with 5+ conditions → Flowchart + Python code
714: - YAML configuration with complex triggers → Keep YAML, add decision tree diagram

177: ## 4. RULES
178: 
179: ### ✅ ALWAYS
180: 
181: 1. **ALWAYS read `references/design-md-format.md` and `references/writing-style-guide.md` before writing DESIGN.md.** These define the v3 Style Reference section specification and the voice/tone rules. No DESIGN.md is conformant without them.
182: 2. **ALWAYS copy every numeric CSS value verbatim from `tokens.json`.** Hex colors, pixel sizes, font weights, box shadows, border radii, spacing values — every number must match `tokens.json` exactly. This is the cardinal fidelity rule.
183: 3. **ALWAYS use 6-digit lowercase hex** for every color in DESIGN.md (e.g., `#1a1a2e`, never `#1A1A2E`, `#333`, `rgb()`, or `hsl()`).
184: 4. **ALWAYS apply stability gates:** L1 and L2 colours in the main token table; L3 colours in the "Current Campaign Colors (Subject to change)" sub-table; L4 tokens excluded entirely.
185: 5. **ALWAYS run `validate.ts` before claiming completion** of any extraction or DESIGN.md edit.
186:    Validation checks hex accuracy against `tokens.json`, v3 Style Reference section completeness, Quick-Start fidelity, and prose provenance.
187:    Every Quick Start hex traces to a token, and `--page-max-width` matches `tokens.json`.
188:    The gate passes only with zero hard failures in the `target`, `schema`, and `provenance` categories.
189:    `valuesScore` and `claimsScore` print as information.
190: 6. **ALWAYS include a dark-mode section ONLY when `tokens.json` contains a detected dark-mode palette.** Never infer, derive, or fabricate a dark palette from the light tokens.
191: 7. **ALWAYS include an accessibility section** drawn from the `tokens.json` a11y data (contrast ratios, focus ring styles, minimum touch-target sizes). If the extractor captured no a11y data, note the absence rather than inventing values.
192: 8. **ALWAYS confirm tool readiness** before any extract/validate/report invocation: `cd backend && npm install && npx playwright install chromium`. The embedded tool requires Node.js and a Playwright Chromium binary.
193: 9. **ALWAYS cite `procedures/design-system-extraction.md` or the no-procedure fallback** before substantial extraction planning, generation, validation, or report output.
194: 10. **ALWAYS, on a brief-only request with no live URL, STOP before producing any Style Reference content.**
195:     The entire response is text only. Choose either:
196:     - Request the live URL to crawl.
197:     - Explicitly state that brief-only authoring is out of scope for this mode, cite `references/authoring-boundary.md` by path, and name the sibling authoring skill `sk-design` as the route.
198:     Cite both `references/authoring-boundary.md` and `assets/source-of-truth-router-card.md` by file path in the response text. Reading them with a tool call does not replace naming them for the user.

200:     A labeled or disclaimed artifact is still forward-authoring. The boundary forbids the artifact itself, not just unlabeled values inside it.
201:     There is no third option or "boundary exception" framing that produces output anyway.

203: ### ⛔ NEVER
204: 
205: 1. **NEVER estimate, round, or invent a hex, pixel, font-weight, shadow, or radius value in DESIGN.md.** Every value must trace back to a token in `tokens.json`. Even trivial-looking values like `1px` borders or `0.25rem` spacing must be confirmed.
206: 2. **NEVER include L4 (content) tokens in DESIGN.md.** These are image-derived or one-off values that do not represent the design system.
207: 3. **NEVER replace the v3 Style Reference format with a freeform structure.**
208:    The named sections are part of the contract that downstream consumers — `sk-code` and AI coding agents — depend on:
209:    - Tokens — Colors/Typography/Spacing & Shapes
210:    - Components
211:    - Do's and Don'ts
212:    - Surfaces
213:    - Elevation
214:    - Layout
215:    - Agent Prompt Guide
216:    - Similar Brands
217:    - Quick Start
218:    Never assert a false system (gradient-as-depth, focus-consistent) that the tokens contradict.
219: 4. **NEVER skip validation before claiming a DESIGN.md is complete.** An unvalidated DESIGN.md is a draft. Validation errors must be resolved before completion.
